points.why: Explicitly labels new reports as inflow, open-bug count as stock, and closures as outflow.
Shows with a numeric example that the backlog keeps growing while inflow exceeds closures even after inflow halves.
Raises whether engineers were moved from fixing to quality work, lowering the closure rate, and treats that as a separate problem to investigate.
Judges the push by the inflow drop and says the backlog turns around once net growth reaches zero.

pitfalls.why: States outright that a halved inflow can still leave the stock rising.
